alignments.note: Causal כִּי as For.
The clause's negation is absorbed into the but of the כִּי אִם fusion below; the ASV writes no separate not, so this לֹא has nothing (rule 22).
כֹּל as all.

כִּי אִם rendered by the single word but: rule 35's named fusion. Neither member uniquely carries the lexeme, so כִּי is the deterministic anchor (rule 6). Recorded noncompositional, with the chapter's other rule-30 fusions.
Construct chain men of death rendered attributively as dead men; follow the ASV (rule 28).
Construct noun men.
The לְ is rendered by before (rule 11).
Suffix as possessive (rule 18).
Host noun lord.
Article takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun king.
Waw rendered by the connective yet, which rule 14 reads off the ASV rather than from a closed list.
Verb with its auxiliary and subject pronoun (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Object marker with no English of its own: the ASV writes the object bare, set thy servant (rule 16).
Suffix as possessive (rule 18).
Host noun servant.
Preposition among (rule 11).
Anarthrous substantival participle: the supplied them that and the tense auxiliary join its unit, since no article morpheme is present to take them (rule 46), headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Nomen rectum of eaters of thy table, with the construct relation recast as at (rule 19); the unit is discontinuous around the suffix's thine own (rule 25).
The ASV intensifies the possessive with own, and the whole emphatic possessive belongs to the suffix, headed on thine (rule 18).

צְדָקָה rendered right.
Waw rendered by the connective therefore, which the ASV writes postpositively; distance from the waw is not evidence against it (rules 14, 51).
The existential יֵשׁ is what makes the clause possessive, so it carries the recasting have; its preposition goes unrepresented and its suffix takes the subject pronoun (rules 43, 40).
The possessive recasting leaves this לְ no English word (rules 40, 43).
Suffix takes the subject pronoun of the recast possessive clause (rules 40, 43).
עוֹד as yet.
The ASV writes no connective for this waw: the clause is recast as a purpose clause opening with that, which belongs to the לְ below (rules 14, 52).
Purpose לְ + infinitive construct recast as a finite clause: the complementizer is what the preposition contributes (rule 52).
The infinitive keeps its supplied subject pronoun and modal (rules 52, 17), headed on the lexical verb.
עוֹד rendered by the two-word any more; head on the word carrying the lexeme (rules 24, 31).
Preposition unto (rule 11).
Article takes the written the (rule 15).
Noun king.

review_notes: Only the status of the כִּי אִם unit changed; its edges and heads are as the verse pass returned them, and no other unit was touched.
Every source and target ID is partitioned exactly once; four unrepresented units (s002, s019, s029, s033) and no added units.

The clause's negation is carried by the but of כִּי אִם rather than by a separate not, which is why לֹא is unrepresented; the competing reading gives but to לֹא and marks כִּי אִם unrepresented, but rule 35 names כִּי אִם as the source of that fusion.
